title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Boston Dynamics Atlas Hand

### The Breakthrough
Boston Dynamics unveiled a redesigned Atlas robot hand that expands from 7 to 13 degrees of freedom, adds a fourth finger and finger‑splay, and embeds larger direct‑drive actuators with replaceable packs for force feedback. The architecture is designed for rugged, low‑cost, mass‑production and mirrors a hand shape suitable for learning from human demonstrations, enabling more versatile tool use.

### The Caveats
The claim of rugged, low‑cost, mass‑producible performance lacks any independent metrics or real‑world testing data.

## GlassGuard Navigation Mapping

### The Breakthrough
GlassGuard fuses foundation‑vision glass masks with structural 3D cues and depth‑free projective checks to reconstruct planar glass surfaces, achieving 85% glass coverage and a 5‑17× reduction in false voxels per frame compared to baselines while mapping on real robots across nine building‑scale scenes.

### The Caveats
No specific baseline methods are named, so the reduction claim lacks a concrete reference point.

## InterEvolve Test‑Time Reward Evolution

### The Breakthrough
InterEvolve equips a pre‑trained humanoid controller with a forward‑backward behavioral model and an LLM‑driven planner that rewrites reward programs on‑the‑fly; the system discovers new loco‑manipulation strategies on a Unitree G1 robot without extra training data.

### The Caveats
The study never benchmarks InterEvolve against existing test‑time adaptation approaches, leaving its advantage unsubstantiated.

## RPG Guided Self‑Improvement

### The Breakthrough
RPG extracts capabilities from offline datasets, generates simulation practice tasks, and iteratively expands a symbolic skill library and system prompt, raising success on 22 held‑out manipulation tasks from 28.6% to 95.0% and achieving full success on 30 real‑world trials across three tasks on a single robot.

### The Caveats
Real‑world validation is limited to three tasks on one robot, with no broader hardware evaluation.

## OpenAI Astra Robot‑Control Model

### The Breakthrough
Astra, a trillion‑parameter LLM, directly outputs precise gripper positions, eliminating a separate low‑level controller, and topped the RoboDojo robot‑control benchmark, surpassing specialized models such as Ω.5 and MolmoAct2.

### The Caveats
Claims rest on informal video demos and a single leaderboard ranking, lacking quantitative hardware tests, latency measurements, or robustness analysis.

## SkeleWAM Skeleton World‑Action Model

### The Breakthrough
SkeleWAM replaces dense visual predictions with a lightweight 3D skeleton and introduces Medoid Action Consensus to infer actions from the skeleton and language instructions, reaching 85.9% success on the LIBERO‑Plus benchmark with only 57.1 M parameters, beating the Cosmos‑Policy baseline.

### The Caveats
Results are demonstrated solely in simulation; no real‑world robot experiments are provided.

## Company Knowledge Bench Retrieval

### The Breakthrough
Kapa’s Company Knowledge Bench offers a 1,000‑case real‑world retrieval set; a simple grep‑based frontier model scores 0.61 while the tuned Kapa Deep reaches 0.65 in about five seconds, using a two‑stage agent pipeline trained on a 170‑case labelled subset.

### The Caveats
Benchmarks are limited to Kapa‑built retrievers with no comparison to public or third‑party systems.

## crowd Pedestrian Behaviour Dataset

### The Breakthrough
The crowd‑dataset pipeline scrapes 33,645 hours of YouTube dashcam video from 238 countries and applies YOLOv11 at scale, producing over 94 k annotated pedestrian video segments for cross‑cultural autonomous‑vehicle safety research.

### The Caveats
No quantitative detection accuracy or baseline comparison is provided, leaving dataset reliability unverified.

## VisionState Home‑Assistant Add‑on

### The Breakthrough
VisionState runs a DINOv2‑based model locally on CPUs, retraining in about one second after a user click, and outputs MQTT sensors for Home Assistant, supporting object, state, and OCR detection without cloud services.

### The Caveats
The project offers no benchmark or accuracy numbers and lacks comparison to existing vision add‑ons.

### Priority
Boston Dynamics' new Atlas hand sets a concrete hardware baseline for mass‑produced, high‑DOF manipulation, making it the most actionable development for today’s robotics community.

### One action
Review the released design specs and simulation models from Boston Dynamics to prototype similar high‑DOF grippers in your own lab.

### What to watch
InterEvolve, RPG, and SkeleWAM all target scalable robot skill acquisition—via reward‑program evolution, self‑improving symbolic libraries, or lightweight skeleton representations. Future releases that validate these approaches on diverse real robots will clarify which paradigm best bridges simulation gains to hardware performance.
